tasks.title: Create LazyVim Bootstrap and Core Configuration Structure
tasks.description: Set up the new init.lua with LazyVim bootstrap pattern and create the lua/config/ directory structure with lazy.lua, options.lua, keymaps.lua, and autocmds.lua files.
tasks.details:
## Implementation Steps

### 1. Update init.lua with LazyVim bootstrap pattern

Replace current init.lua content with LazyVim bootstrap:

```lua
-- Bootstrap lazy.nvim and LazyVim
local lazypath = vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/lazy/lazy.nvim"
if not (vim.uv or vim.loop).fs_stat(lazypath) then
  local lazyrepo = "https://github.com/folke/lazy.nvim.git"
  local out = vim.fn.system({ "git", "clone", "--filter=blob:none", "--branch=stable", lazyrepo, lazypath })
  if vim.v.shell_error ~= 0 then
    vim.api.nvim_echo({ { "Failed to clone lazy.nvim:\n", "ErrorMsg" }, { out, "WarningMsg" } }, true, {})
  end
end
vim.opt.rtp:prepend(lazypath)

-- LazyVim global options
vim.g.mapleader = " "
vim.g.maplocalleader = "\\"
vim.g.colorscheme = "nvchad" -- Keep NvChad UI mode initially

require("lazy").setup({
  spec = {
    { "LazyVim/LazyVim", import = "lazyvim.plugins" },
    { import = "lazyvim.plugins.extras.coding.blink" },
    -- Import enabled extras from lazyvim.json
    { import = "plugins" },
  },
  defaults = { lazy = true },
  install = { colorscheme = { "tokyonight", "haiku" } },
  checker = { enabled = not vim.g.is_windows },
  performance = {
    rtp = {
      disabled_plugins = {
        "gzip", "tarPlugin", "tohtml", "tutor", "zipPlugin",
      },
    },
  },
})
```

### 2. Create lua/config/ directory structure

Create the following files:

**lua/config/lazy.lua** - LazyVim specific lazy.nvim configuration (merged from lua/core/lazy.lua)

**lua/config/options.lua** - Merge options from:
- lua/options.lua (base NvChad options)
- lua/serpro69/options.lua (custom options)
- Add LazyVim-specific globals (vim.g.lazyvim_picker, vim.g.lazyvim_cmp, etc.)

**lua/config/keymaps.lua** - Merge keymaps from:
- lua/mappings.lua (base keymaps - ~334 lines)
- lua/serpro69/mappings.lua (custom keymaps - ~65 lines)
- Convert from NvChad tabufline navigation to LazyVim buffer navigation

**lua/config/autocmds.lua** - Merge autocmds from:
- lua/core/autocommands.lua
- lua/core/serpro69/autocommands.lua

### 3. Create lazyvim.json for extras

```json
{
  "extras": [
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.ai.copilot",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.coding.blink",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.coding.luasnip",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.dap.core",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.editor.flash",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.editor.harpoon2",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.formatting.conform",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.docker",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.go",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.java",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.json",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.kotlin",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.markdown",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.nix",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.terraform",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.typescript",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.lang.yaml",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.linting.eslint",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.test.core",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.ui.treesitter-context",
    "lazyvim.plugins.extras.util.project"
  ],
  "news": {
    "lazyvim": "12"
  },
  "version": 7
}
```

### Key Considerations
- Preserve vim.g.is_windows detection
- Keep VSCode conditional loading if needed
- Maintain vim.version() >= 11 compatibility hack
- Update type annotations from NvPluginSpec to LazySpec

tasks.title: Migrate NvChad UI Components as Optional Colorscheme Plugin
tasks.description: Configure NvChad as an optional plugin that provides statusline, tabufline, and base46 themes when vim.g.colorscheme is set to 'nvchad', preserving the custom statusline modules (harpoon_indicator, pomo_timer).
tasks.details:
## Implementation Steps

### 1. Create lua/plugins/colorscheme/nvchad.lua

```lua
---@type LazySpec
return {
  {
    "NvChad/NvChad",
    enabled = vim.g.colorscheme == "nvchad",
    lazy = false,
    branch = "v2.5",
    import = "nvchad.plugins",
    config = function()
      require("options") -- Load NvChad default options
    end,
  },
  { "nvzone/volt", enabled = vim.g.colorscheme == "nvchad" },
  { "nvzone/minty", enabled = vim.g.colorscheme == "nvchad" },
  -- Disable LazyVim UI components when using NvChad
  { "nvim-lualine/lualine.nvim", enabled = vim.g.colorscheme ~= "nvchad" },
  { "akinsho/bufferline.nvim", enabled = vim.g.colorscheme ~= "nvchad" },
}
```

### 2. Migrate chadrc.lua to new location

Keep lua/chadrc.lua with existing configuration but update requires:
- Keep statusline modules from serpro69/chadrc_aux.lua
- Keep harpoon_indicator function
- Keep pomo_timer function
- Keep theme_toggle and custom highlight overrides
- Keep Mason packages list

### 3. Migrate custom themes

Copy lua/themes/eldritch.lua and lua/themes/github_dark_dimmed.lua unchanged.
These work with NvChad's base46 theming system.

### 4. Update serpro69/chadrc_aux.lua

Keep this file as-is since it provides:
- themes_customs with highlight overrides
- base46_overrides for theme configuration
- Custom statusline modules (harpoon_statusline_indicator, filename, git_custom, modified, bufnr, pomo_timer)
- statusline and tabufline helper objects

### 5. Create LazyVim colorscheme fallback

```lua
-- lua/plugins/colorscheme/init.lua
---@type LazySpec
return {
  {
    "folke/tokyonight.nvim",
    enabled = vim.g.colorscheme ~= "nvchad",
    lazy = false,
    priority = 1000,
    opts = {},
  },
}
```

### Key Files to Preserve
- lua/serpro69/chadrc_aux.lua (statusline customizations)
- lua/chadrc.lua (NvChad configuration)
- lua/themes/*.lua (custom color schemes)
- lua/highlights.lua (highlight overrides)
- lua/core/statusline/ (statusline modules)
- lua/core/tabufline/ (tabufline modules)

tasks.title: Migrate Formatter and Linter Configuration
tasks.description: Convert conform.lua and nvim-lint.lua to LazyVim extension pattern, preserving custom formatters (ktfmt for Kotlin, yamlfmt for YAML) and linters (eslint_d, shellcheck, ktlint).
tasks.details:
## Implementation Steps

### 1. Create lua/plugins/lsp/conform.lua (extending LazyVim extra)

```lua
---@type LazySpec
return {
  "stevearc/conform.nvim",
  opts = function(_, opts)
    -- Extend LazyVim's default formatters_by_ft
    opts.formatters_by_ft = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", opts.formatters_by_ft or {}, {
      php = { "pint" },
      blade = { "blade-formatter" },
      cpp = { "clang_format" },
      c = { "clang_format" },
      go = { "gofumpt" },
      yaml = { "yamlfmt" },
      css = { "prettier" },
      html = { "prettier" },
      json = { "prettier" },
      javascript = { "prettier" },
      javascriptreact = { "prettier" },
      typescript = { "prettier" },
      typescriptreact = { "prettier" },
      vue = { "prettier" },
      kotlin = { "ktfmt" },
      graphql = { "prettier" },
      less = { "prettier" },
      scss = { "prettier" },
      flow = { "prettier" },
    })

    -- Custom format_after_save logic
    opts.format_after_save = function(bufnr)
      if vim.g.disable_autoformat or vim.b[bufnr].disable_autoformat then
        return
      end
      local bufname = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_name(bufnr)
      if bufname:match("/node_modules/") then
        return
      end
      return { timeout_ms = 500, lsp_format = "fallback" }
    end

    -- Custom formatter configuration for ktfmt
    opts.formatters = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", opts.formatters or {}, {
      ktfmt = {
        append_args = { "--kotlinlang-style" },
      },
    })

    return opts
  end,
}
```

### 2. Create lua/plugins/lsp/nvim-lint.lua

Note: Current config has nvim-lint disabled. Preserve the configuration but keep it disabled:

```lua
---@type LazySpec
return {
  "mfussenegger/nvim-lint",
  enabled = false, -- Currently disabled in original config
  opts = {
    linters_by_ft = {
      javascript = { "eslint_d" },
      javascriptreact = { "eslint_d" },
      typescript = { "eslint_d" },
      typescriptreact = { "eslint_d" },
      markdown = { "markdownlint" },
      sh = { "shellcheck" },
      yaml = { "yamllint" },
      kotlin = { "ktlint" },
    },
  },
  config = function(_, opts)
    local lint = require("lint")
    lint.linters_by_ft = opts.linters_by_ft
    vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd({ "CursorHold", "CursorHoldI" }, {
      callback = function()
        lint.try_lint()
      end,
    })
  end,
}
```

### 3. Delete obsolete files

- Delete lua/plugins/lsp/configs/conform.lua (after migration)
- Delete lua/plugins/lsp/configs/nvim-lint.lua (after migration)

### Key Considerations
- LazyVim's conform extra already provides basic configuration
- We're extending it with custom formatters, not replacing
- Preserve the format_after_save logic that disables for node_modules
- Keep ktfmt's kotlinlang-style argument

tasks.title: Migrate Custom Modules and Notifications
tasks.description: Migrate serpro69/notify.lua (LSP/DAP progress notifications with spinners), serpro69/commands.lua (ObsidianFormatAIOutput), and integrate custom notification handling.
tasks.details:
## Implementation Steps

### 1. Migrate serpro69/notify.lua

This file provides custom LSP progress notifications with spinner animations. LazyVim uses Snacks.notifier by default, but we can keep nvim-notify for compatibility.

**Option A: Keep nvim-notify and custom notifications**

Create lua/plugins/ui/nvim-notify.lua:

```lua
---@type LazySpec
return {
  "rcarriga/nvim-notify",
  opts = {
    timeout = 3000,
    max_height = function()
      return math.floor(vim.o.lines * 0.75)
    end,
    max_width = function()
      return math.floor(vim.o.columns * 0.75)
    end,
    on_open = function(win)
      vim.api.nvim_win_set_config(win, { zindex = 100 })
    end,
  },
  init = function()
    -- Replace default notify
    vim.notify = require("notify")
  end,
}
```

Then load the custom LSP progress handler in config/autocmds.lua or keep in serpro69/notify.lua:
- LSP `$/progress` handler with spinner animation
- Macro recording notifications
- Custom notification styling

**Option B: Use Snacks.notifier (LazyVim default)**

Migrate spinner logic to work with Snacks or accept simpler notifications.

### 2. Migrate serpro69/commands.lua

Move ObsidianFormatAIOutput command to config/autocmds.lua or keep in separate file:

```lua
-- In lua/config/autocmds.lua or serpro69/commands.lua
vim.api.nvim_create_user_command("ObsidianFormatAIOutput", function(opts)
  local start_line = opts.line1
  local end_line = opts.line2

  if not opts.range then
    start_line = 1
    end_line = vim.fn.line("$")
  end

  -- Remove extra spaces after list markers
  vim.cmd(string.format("%d,%ds/\\v^(\\s*[*|-]|\\d+\\.?|\\w+\\.?)\\s+/\\1 /g", start_line, end_line))
  -- Prepend "> " to each line
  vim.cmd(string.format("%d,%ds/^/> /g", start_line, end_line))
end, {
  range = true,
  desc = "Format markdown output from AI for obsidian note",
})
```

### 3. Update init.lua or config to load modules

In config/autocmds.lua or a custom loader:

```lua
-- Load custom commands
if vim.fn.isdirectory(vim.fn.stdpath("config") .. "/lua/serpro69") == 1 then
  require("serpro69.commands")
  require("serpro69.notify")
end
```

### 4. Preserve NvChad notification integration

If using NvChad UI mode, notifications work with nvim-notify.
If using LazyVim UI, consider whether to keep nvim-notify or migrate to Snacks.

### Files to keep/migrate:
- lua/serpro69/notify.lua - LSP progress with spinners, macro notifications
- lua/serpro69/commands.lua - ObsidianFormatAIOutput command
- lua/core/commands.lua - Other custom commands
- lua/core/serpro69/autocommands.lua - Custom autocommands

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Create lua/plugins/editor/nvim-tree.lua

Move from navigation/ and integrate Avante keymaps from plugins_aux.lua:

```lua
---@type LazySpec
return {
  "nvim-tree/nvim-tree.lua",
  cmd = { "NvimTreeToggle", "NvimTreeFocus", "NvimTreeFindFile" },
  keys = {
    { "<leader>e", "<cmd>NvimTreeToggle<cr>", desc = "Explorer (nvim-tree)" },
  },
  opts = {
    -- Your existing opts
  },
  config = function(_, opts)
    local api = require("nvim-tree.api")
    
    -- Custom on_attach with Avante integration
    opts.on_attach = function(bufnr)
      local function opts_fn(desc)
        return { desc = "nvim-tree: " .. desc, buffer = bufnr, noremap = true, silent = true, nowait = true }
      end
      
      -- Apply keymaps from plugins_aux.lua
      require("serpro69.plugins_aux").keymaps.nvim_tree(api, opts_fn, bufnr)
    end
    
    require("nvim-tree").setup(opts)
  end,
}
```

### 2. Create lua/plugins/editor/flash.lua (extending LazyVim extra)

```lua
---@type LazySpec
return {
  "folke/flash.nvim",
  opts = function(_, opts)
    -- Extend LazyVim's flash configuration
    opts.labels = "asdfghjklqwertyuiopzxcvbnm" -- Custom labels if different
    opts.search = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", opts.search or {}, {
      -- Custom search settings
    })
    return opts
  end,
}
```

### 3. Handle other editor plugins

```lua
}
```

**legendary.lua** → util/legendary.lua:

```lua
  "mrjones2014/legendary.nvim",
  priority = 10000,
  lazy = false,
  opts = {
    -- Existing options

}
```

### 4. Handle LazyVim's neo-tree vs nvim-tree

LazyVim uses neo-tree by default. Options:

**Option A: Disable neo-tree, use nvim-tree**

### 6. Preserve custom treesitter additions

```lua
  "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter",

      "go", "hcl", "kotlin", "make", "terraform", "twig", "yaml",
```
